text: With respect to traditional resistance exercise, there is evidence that serial hypertrophy occurs to an extent during the early stages of participation. Seynnes and colleagues (207) reported a 9.9% increase in fascicle length in a group of recreationally active men and women after a 35-day high-intensity resistance training program. However, a longer-term study by Blazevich and colleagues (30) found that fascicle length changes were specific to the initial 5 weeks of resistance training, and that adaptations did not persist beyond this period. Evidence suggests that altering the style of training may influence changes in serial hypertrophy.
